evidence: The origin of the acid sound from a secondhand TB-303 operated without its manual is documented in many interviews with DJ Pierre and the other members of Phuture.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: The pattern of notes barely changes for twelve minutes. Everything that moves is the filter, opening and closing, and the resonance screaming at the top. Listen for the slide between notes, which is the machine doing a thing a bass player would do, badly, and brilliantly.

explanation: The 303 failed as a product, which made it cheap. Phuture got one without instructions and turned the knobs while it was playing. A whole genre is named after the sound that came out. It is the clearest case of a machine as the hero of the story: failure made it cheap, cheap made it reachable, and people with no stake in how it was meant to be used made the genre.
